design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that after baseline assessment participants "were randomized to one of two conditions: problem orientation treatment or control," so this is a randomized parallel-group trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were explicitly randomized and reported baseline outcome differences were consistent with chance, but the sequence-generation method and allocation-concealment procedures were not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Following the interview, participants completed several self-report questionnaires and were randomized to one of two conditions: problem orientation treatment or control.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants likely knew which video content they received, and the report does not describe blinding, intervention adherence, contamination, or a clearly specified intention-to-treat estimand, although both groups received time-matched videos and latent growth modeling incorporated repeated observations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Those assigned to the control condition received a video matched for time that focused on current health issues such as proper diet, exercise, and sleep habits but with no reference to coping strategies or methods for dealing with health issues.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome attrition was substantial and increased to 59% at the last reported follow-up; similar dropout rates between arms and latent growth modeling do not establish that missingness was unrelated to outcomes or that estimates were unbiased.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The dropout rate increased across the follow-ups (FU; FU1 = 13% attrition; FU2 = 18% attrition; FU3 = 33% attrition; FU4 = 59% attrition), which was largely due to individuals leaving campus following quarter breaks.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcomes were assessed identically with established self-report instruments, but participants likely knew their assigned condition and could therefore have reported subjective suicidal ideation and depression differently after the intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Follow-up evaluations were scheduled at 1 week, 2 weeks, and 1 month following the baseline assessment. These assessments included completion of self-report measures related to suicide, depression, hopelessness, and problem solving.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper states a priori hypotheses and contrasts, but no preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and several outcomes, time points, continuous growth analyses, and post hoc categorical BSS analyses created scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The a priori contrasts in this analysis tested the null hypothesis of (a) no difference in rates of suicide ideation between the prevention and the control groups at baseline or across the 2-month follow-up period and (b) no difference in levels of problem solving between the prevention and the control groups.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven primarily by substantial missing outcome data, reaching 59% attrition at the final reported follow-up without convincing evidence that missingness could not bias results. Additional concerns arise from unreported sequence concealment, likely participant awareness with subjective self-reported outcomes, and absence of a preregistered analysis plan.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that eligible students were stratified by self-harm ideation score and randomly assigned to the structured-writing or control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although assignment was described as stratified and random, the sequence-generation and concealment methods were not reported, and participants were recruited after being told their assigned group, creating differential post-randomization participation and exclusions that could compromise group comparability.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: They were stratified and randomly assigned to the intervention or the control group, based on their self-harm ideation score and were requested to participate in the study, after explaining the criteria of the group they were assigned.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants necessarily knew whether they performed writing, the control received no attention-matched activity, and the analysis was not intention-to-treat because randomized nonparticipants, no-shows, and participants with baseline SHI scores of zero were excluded after assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: As a result, data of 10 participants in the intervention group...and 12 participants in the control group...were analyzed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 22 of 56 randomized candidates were analyzed, with substantial post-randomization losses due to refusal, no-shows, and exclusions, and no analysis demonstrated that missing outcomes were unlikely to bias the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of these, 33 students (18 in the intervention group and 15 in the control group) agreed to participate. domain_judgments.rationale: All outcomes were participant-reported in an unblinded behavioral intervention, so knowledge of assignment could influence responses, and the primary self-harm ideation instrument was newly created without reliability or validity data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The last limitation concerns the index of selfharm that was used, which was specially developed for this study. To date, there are no data on the reliability or the validity of this index.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or preregistered analysis plan was reported, and several outcomes, time points, within-group tests, interaction tests, and multiple comparisons allowed scope for selective reporting, although the named outcomes and descriptive results were presented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Effects of structured writing were also evaluated using one of two statistical analyses : The Friedman test...and a repeated measures Analyses of Variance...

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because post-randomization recruitment and substantial exclusions undermined randomization and produced major missing-data and non-ITT concerns. Unblinded self-reported outcomes, including an unvalidated self-harm scale, add serious measurement bias.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports individual random assignment to BMM or wait-list control using random numbers generated in SPSS.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random-number procedure was reported, but allocation concealment was not described and baseline sleep efficiency differed significantly between groups, leaving some concern about implementation of randomization.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Sixty four participants were recruited for the present study after the interviewing and screening process, and were randomly assigned to one of the two groups using a random number generated and randomly grouped by SPSS.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intervention was readily distinguishable from no treatment, adherence varied, the control group's engagement in related interventions was not monitored, and the analysis excluded four randomized participants rather than following intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Finally, during the experiment, we did not monitor the control group to ensure they were not engaging in any related interventions, although they were asked not to, if it was not a crisis situation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Four of 64 randomized participants were excluded from the reported analyses and three post-test actigraphy values were missing due to instrument failure, with no sensitivity analysis or evidence that missingness could not bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Sixty participants who completed all group sessions and with an absence of less than three self-help sessions were included in current study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although trial registration was reported, no prespecified analysis plan is provided, many outcomes and analyses were tested, and conclusions emphasized favorable within-group changes despite nonsignificant between-group changes, creating substantial risk of selective emphasis or analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: However, we did not found significant advantage of BMM group over control group.

design_rationale: Although described as quasiexperimental and based on purposive recruitment, the Methods explicitly state that the 86 enrolled participants were randomly assigned to the two intervention groups.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated in blocks of three to DBT-ZYT, supportive group therapy, or wait-list using a computer program.

domain_judgments.rationale: Post-treatment attrition was about 13–16% and was strongly associated with worse baseline outcomes, while last-observation-carried-forward imputation relies on implausible stability assumptions and may bias intervention estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: There were also significant differences on all of the baseline assessments between completers (n = 83) and noncompleters (n = 14).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were self-reported by participants who necessarily knew their assigned intervention, so expectations and social desirability could differentially influence measurement despite blinded administration.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prospective statistical analysis plan is reported, and numerous scales, subscales, time points, repeated-measures analyses, and paired comparisons created scope for selective reporting despite stated Bonferroni correction.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by outcome-dependent attrition handled with last-observation-carried-forward and by unblinded participant-reported outcomes that could be influenced by intervention expectations. design_rationale: Participants were explicitly allocated after baseline using an independent, computer-generated randomization list stratified by school, with allocation concealed until participant details were entered.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated by an independent statistician, stratified by school, and concealed until participant details were entered; although prior suicide attempts were imbalanced, the primary baseline SIQ scores were closely balanced and the small sample makes a chance imbalance plausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This was done via an online randomisation computer program set up by an independent statistician (HPY). The program did not allow knowledge of treatment next to be allocated before the participant details were entered into the computer.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and school staff necessarily knew assignment, intervention adherence was limited, and co-interventions differed between groups, although analysis was by original assignment and there is no clear evidence that deviations arose because of the trial context.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because of the nature of the intervention, it was not possible for school staff to be blind to intervention... Analysis was by original assignment groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary-outcome data were missing for 40% of randomized participants at 22 weeks, with differential attrition of 50% in the intervention group versus 29.2% in controls and no evidence that estimates were robust to missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The 22-week assessment was completed by 17 and 13 participants in the control and intervention groups, respectively, with a corresponding dropout rate of 29.2% and 50%.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome of the study was reduced suicidal ideation as measured by the Suicidal Ideation Questionnaire (SIQ)... All self-report outcome measures with the exception of the CDRS-R were administered online.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, its protocol was published, the primary outcome and follow-up times were specified, and the stated mixed-effects comparison was reported, with no evident selective choice among eligible analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial has been registered (ACTRN12613000864729; 5 August 2013), and the protocol for the trial has been published.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by substantial and differential missing outcome data at 22 weeks without evidence that the result was insensitive to missingness. Additional concerns arise from unblinded self-reported outcomes and possible deviations/co-intervention differences, despite a sound randomization process and prospective registration.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 73 eligible students were randomly assigned to IPT-A-IN or treatment as usual, although the method used to generate and conceal the allocation sequence was not described.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random assignment was stated, but the sequence-generation and allocation-concealment methods were not reported, and a baseline anxiety imbalance was noted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: a total of 73 depressed students with suicidal risk were recruited into the intervention program, and they were randomly assigned to the IPT-A-IN and the TAU programs.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and providers could not be blinded to these behavioral interventions, TAU intensity was irregular, co-interventions were permitted, and the analysis was not explicitly intention-to-treat, although major differential deviations were not evident.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the courses of both intervention models, combining medication or family education was allowed if the psychiatrist suggested it.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three participants in the TAU group dropped out.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Assessment tools were self-report scales, therefore, evaluators would remind students who had omissions in the questionnaire and help to calculate the total scores.

Key uncertainties are the unreported sequence generation and concealment, unclear handling of three TAU dropouts, unblinded subjective self-report outcomes, possible deviations/co-interventions, and absence of a reported prespecified protocol or analysis plan.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomized to CAMS or TAU using an adaptive biased-coin allocation design.

domain_judgments.rationale: A valid adaptive biased-coin randomization method was reported and baseline variables were generally balanced, but concealment of the allocation sequence until assignment was not described and age showed a near-imbalance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Both treatments were balanced in terms of psychotropic medication use, presence of a past suicide attempt, and gender utilizing an adaptive-biased coin design (Wei & Lachin, 1988).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating counselors could not be blinded in this psychotherapy trial, but fidelity monitoring showed separation of the interventions and weekly outcomes were analyzed in the intent-to-treat sample; handling of post-treatment outcomes was less clearly intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: HLM/HGLM data from all participants (the intent-to-treat sample) were utilized with weekly measures.

domain_judgments.rationale: Treatment dropout was 22.6% and only 51 of 62 participants contributed some post-treatment data, although attrition did not differ significantly by group and pattern-mixture sensitivity analyses supported the weekly depression and suicidal-ideation findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pattern mixture models (Hedeker & Gibbons, 1997) indicated that analyses on intervention effects for depression and suicidal ideation were not sensitive to missing data patterns.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although independent baseline/post assessors were blinded and several measures were validated, key weekly outcomes were participant-reported in an unblinded behavioral trial and clinician CGI outcomes were rated by the unblinded treating counselors using study-developed suicidality scales, creating substantial potential for differential measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At the end of each treatment session, counselors rated 1) clients’ overall improvement in suicidal risk since baseline... and 2) clients’ current overall severity of suicidality.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration was identified, but no prespecified analysis plan was documented here, alpha was not adjusted despite numerous outcomes, models, covariates, moderators, and contrasts, and the report emphasized selected significant weekly and subgroup results, indicating substantial analytic and reporting flexibility.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Alpha was set at .05 to preserve power.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because key weekly outcomes could be influenced by knowledge of treatment assignment, especially clinician ratings made by treating counselors, and extensive outcome, model, covariate, and moderator testing without a clearly documented prespecified analysis plan creates high risk of selective reporting. Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment and appreciable missing post-treatment data.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly randomly assigned to DBT or O-TAU using a computerized urn randomization procedure that balanced specified baseline prognostic factors.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and treating clinicians necessarily knew the psychotherapy received, dropout was substantial, and treatment exposure differed in group-session attendance, although ITT mixed-effects analyses and sensitivity models addressing retention and treatment hours reduced concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Approximately 35% of the DBT group (11/31) and 47% of the O-TAU group (15/32) dropped out before completing 7 months of therapy... DBT participants attended significantly more group sessions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Treatment dropout and incomplete longitudinal assessments were substantial enough to create potential missing-data bias, although mixed models, pattern-mixture analyses, active follow-up of dropouts, and conservative coding in clinical-significance analyses provided some reassurance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Every effort was made to recruit participants for assessments, including dropouts, and financial incentives were offered for the 12- ($25) and 18-month ($75) assessments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated measures were applied across groups and interview assessors were blinded with good reliability, but major outcomes such as suicidality, depression, and social adjustment were participant-reported and could be influenced by participants' knowledge of psychotherapy assignment.

design_rationale: The procedure explicitly states that Experimenter 2 randomly assigned participants to one of three writing conditions.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Then Experimenter 2 administered the pretest questions ... randomly assigned participants to one of the three conditions, and gave them a sealed envelope containing their day 1 writing instructions.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 98 of 121 randomized participants completed all phases, the primary longitudinal analyses used an even smaller complete-case sample, and noncompleters had significantly greater baseline depression and external pressure, making outcome-dependent missingness plausible.

domain_judgments.rationale: Validated self-report depression and suicidality measures were administered consistently, but participants were aware of condition and the follow-up was self-completed at home, so subjective outcome reports could have been influenced by intervention knowledge or setting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Another limitation was that the followup questionnaires were mailed and completed at home rather than in the laboratory.

domain_judgments.rationale: No preregistration or prespecified analysis plan is reported, and numerous outcome measures, subscales, time points, transformations, and alternative groupings provided substantial analytic flexibility.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Therefore, the data from the two experimental groups were combined into one experimental group to assess whether the combined experimental group would produce significant findings compared to the control group.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven chiefly by substantial complete-case attrition with evidence that noncompleters were more depressed and stressed at baseline. Additional concerns arise from incompletely reported randomization/concealment, lack of intention-to-treat analysis, unblinded subjective outcomes, and no reported prespecified analysis plan.
